name: (none)
role: Not yet given a real state - `class_counter` (`+0x2E`) only increments "for every unit whose state is not 0" (see the unit record), consistent with 0 meaning "just allocated, not yet dispatched" rather than an ordinary idle state.

name: idle hand-off
role: Initial state for a person with no active behaviour yet; on an RNG-timed expiry hands off to its own per-type ongoing default via table 0x5A7064 (wildman -> 8, angel -> 28, everyone else -> 10). See "Idle behaviour: the idle hand-off: state 1, then state 10".

name: drowning
role: Entered from the universal life-step when the fine-grained per-pixel drowning check (0x4EEFF0) is true; the state's own per-turn body has not been independently traced (only the entry predicate). See "Drowning".

name: death
role: Universal death for any class-1 person, not preach-specific; reached only from the life-step at life<=0. Pushes the dying person onto the universal spirit-rise handoff slot (0x892443), spawns a class-7 death-puff effect and a class-10 spirit-rise controller. See "Death and the spirit rise".

name: idle near a reference unit
role: Generic "idle-fidget beside a paired unit" (own `+0x72` reference, latched from the setter). Reused by at least two unreconciled subsystems: wildmen idling beside a found tree/plant or "noticed" unit (0x4D48E0/0x4D66E0 set the pairing, longer-lived), and the player-issued preach order (0x43C7A0), which sets its target to this SAME state with a short, fixed `+0x70` timer (0x28, 40 ticks/3.3s, armed once, no re-arm found anywhere in this handler) and also stamps `target+0xA7 = 0x28` (the generic, still not fully pinned "busy" field) at the moment of entry. Every tick while the reference is live and within 120 units on both axes: faces it (every 8th tick) and rolls an idle-fidget-animation-variant via the per-type odds table 0x5A7067 (see 0x5A7064's own row); if the reference goes too far away this tick just no-ops (no revert); timer expiry or a dead/invalid reference falls back unconditionally to the per-type default (table 0x5A7064, shaman special-cased to 0x27) - never writes the person's own state onward itself otherwise. **Re-read this session chasing "Preacher conversion"'s kind-33/state-23 reconciliation: confirmed exhaustively this state never transitions to 23 or connects to `preacher_strike_scan` in any way - the two "preacher" mechanisms are genuinely independent, not a tracing gap. The actual link between a manual preach order and a real conversion is elsewhere (the preacher's own concurrent auto-scan pre-empting its own order) - see pop3-rev-analysis.md "Preacher conversion".**

name: walking to the shore
role: Wildman-only: walks toward a shore-shaped cell found by the state-8 fallback search (0x4D4A00); 0x4D66E0 runs every turn en route to "notice" a nearby scenery head, a vehicle, or another tribe's person (-> state 34).

name: wildman idle tick
role: Wildman-only (type 1) periodic idle check, reached from state 1's own per-type hand-off: tries a tree/plant search (0x4D48E0) first, falls back to the shore search (0x4D4A00) on failure.

name: carrying out an order (order_execute)
role: The ordinary "run my current command group" state; the per-type default-on-expiry for braves through shamans (table 0x5A7064). A fight or pre-fight (states 25/29) pauses this without ever releasing the order - the SAME original order resumes exactly where it left off the moment the person drops out of the fight. See "Command groups".

name: idle/fidget cycle
role: A generic idle/fidget cycle: sub-state (`+0x2D`) alternates 1<->2 with an RNG 4-11 turn timer at `+0xAA`. Traced and ruled out as a "defends by preaching" mechanism. `0x434610`'s own row calls out a person finishing entering a building as "person state 0xA/0xE" - possibly the same state reused for "now idling inside", not reconciled with this reading.

name: idle at the shore
role: Wildman-only "drinking" stop, reached from state 6 on arrival at its shore destination; cycles an object/prop sub-state in [8..19] via `0x4D4040`, falls back to the per-type default on timer expiry.

name: tumbling / ground recovery
role: NOT the airborne ballistic flight itself (no velocity/height field +0x49/+0x4B/+0x4D/+0x41 is read anywhere in this function - that physics runs in the separate universal per-unit step, 0x4E6D1D/0x4E6D6D) - this is the GROUND recovery choreography that follows it, confirmed live (a tribe-1 brave hit by Blast enters this state the instant BLOWN, +0xC bit 0x80000, is set). Own sub-state (+0x2D) is a 0/1/2 arrival check (48-unit then 216-unit thresholds against a reference position, meaning unconfirmed) feeding an 8-way jump table (sub-states 3-10): picks a clear nearby cell via an 8-direction offset table (0x895ED9, default 0x895EF1) and moves there (0x4E9DD0); waits randomized timers (+0x70, 4-31 turns, LCG 0x89D178). **The "is this candidate spot OK" check, 0x4D5420, is now traced and confirmed NOT building-aware**: it walks the cell's own linked list (0x8A03E4) filtering strictly for class-1 (person) entries, checking only per-type terrain-climbability (WALK_ALT_DIFF2, movement-profile table 0x5A7B90+0x10, same field state 33 uses) and collision with another live person already claiming the same spot - a building (class 2) on that cell is simply invisible to this check. The sibling function in the initial arrival dispatch, 0x4D5120, is more involved and surfaces one new unconfirmed lead: a per-CELL linked-list HEADER flag (`[cell_list_head+0x1]` bit 0x2, not a per-object field) that, when set, triggers a re-place via 0x4044B0 - plausibly "this cell holds something solid" (a building footprint is the obvious guess, not confirmed). **Resolved, same session, by tracing the physics/landing step itself (0x4E6D00/ground() 0x44E940, see functions.tsv's own rows)**: landing on a building gets no special handling at all - ground() is a pure terrain-height interpolation with no building/class check, so a thrown person always lands at raw terrain height on that cell regardless of any building there; there just isn't a building-awareness mechanism anywhere in this whole chain. **Correction: +0x78 is NOT a trailing-effect counter (an earlier pass of this row wrongly equated it with state 26's own +0xA4 counter) - the Reference already documents +0x78 as a person's plain CARRIED WOOD amount.** The two checks on it here (threshold <1) just pick the matching Idle/Walk vs. holding-wood/Walk-with-wood pose pair (see animation note below); separately, once the first wait timer expires with wood still carried, it spawns a class-5 type-0xB debris effect once per exactly 100 wood decremented from +0x78 (one standard wood load) until 0 - reads as dropping/spilling carried wood in a puff per load while settling, not a generic effect burst (the same +0x78-by-100 pattern, unexplained at the time, also appears in "Preacher conversion"'s sub-state 4 - likely the same wood-drop mechanic there too). NOT ACTUALLY OBSERVED LIVE: the one live trial never logged +0x78/wood, so whether this branch (holding-wood pose, wood-drop puffs) fired for that specific brave is unknown - needs a wood-carrying brave specifically. Every 32 turns while grounded, two more LCG rolls can kick it back into sub-state 6 (~13/32) or 10 (~3/64), both also setting flags+0xC bit 0x40000000 (the same bit cheat.md's live drowning trace found on entering the water-sink sequence - looks like a general pose-variant bit here, not confirmed water-exclusive) - this randomness is why live substates wander non-monotonically (4→5→10→5→6→7…) instead of counting through a fixed sequence. Sub-state 7 ("getting up") rerolls a fresh facing/timer before looping back. Exit: two epilogues return the per-type default state via the same table 0x5A7064 state 1 (0x4D3386) uses, one a fixed state 0x27 (39, shaman debug-mode override, same pattern as 0x518560). Ghidra's function range for 0x4D73E0 (claimed end 0x4D80B9) is wrong - 0x4D7FD0 inside that range is actually the death/spirit-rise record push (state 3's own mechanism), a separate function. **Animations resolved this session, directly from the exe's static data (0x5A6D50/0x5A6858, "Fight"'s own `[action×9+type]` table at 0x4D3FF0, cross-checked against 7 already-known action values, all matching)**: no dedicated "down" sprite - calls 0x4D3FF0 with actions 1/5 (already-documented Walk/Walk-with-wood, picked by the +0x78 wood check above) while moving to the picked spot, and 0/4 while settling, resolving to plain Idle (action 0, VSTART 6/53) and VSTART 10 ("standing still, holding wood", brave-specific, action 4, likewise wood-gated) - both already named in open-populous animations.md. So this whole recovery window most likely looks like an ordinary idle/standing (or holding-wood, if carrying any) person that just isn't taking orders, plus a few dropped-wood puffs if it had wood - not a visibly prolonged "struggling on the ground" animation. This static table-reading is independently cross-checked against 7 already-known action values (all matched exactly) but NOT itself confirmed against this specific live trial. See open-populous pop3-rev-analysis.md "Tumbling and ground recovery" / "A blasted person fighting back".

name: scorched by a blast (forced run, "panics")
handler: 0x4D3832 (per-turn), 0x4D2D74 (entry, in `init_unit_class_1`/0x4D2740's own per-state ENTER dispatch, `switchD_004d290b` caseD_1a)
role: **Correction to this row's own earlier pass, same investigation thread, continued**: the previous note ("purely cosmetic... no movement") checked only the per-turn TICK body (0x4D3832, which does just play the ambient-crackle sound 0x51 and count down the trailing-effect visual) and missed that `init_unit_class_1` (0x4D2740) has a SEPARATE per-state ENTER dispatch (`switchD_004d290b`, the same two-dispatch architecture already confirmed for class 10 in `init_unit_class_10`/0x500E20's own row) - its case 0x1a (state 26) runs ONCE on entry and: detaches any reference pairing (`0x4D4040`, `0x445750`), sets speed `+0x5F = 0x6E` (110), sets the duration timer `+0x70 = 0x40` (64 turns), then rolls a fresh random heading via the standard `0x89D178` LCG and writes it to the facing field `+0x57` (masked to `0x7FF`, 0-2047), also setting `+0xC` bits `0x80`/`0x1000` (the same two bits "on fire"/state 31's own entry, `0x4D8FFA`, sets - a shared "forced random movement" flag pair). **This is a real, confirmed, code-level "runs at a random heading at speed 110 for 64 turns" effect** - almost exactly open-populous pop3-rev-analysis.md's old uncited "Panic (person state 0x1A)" description, just not a separate state from "scorched by a blast", not literally called that in any symbol, and with no scream sound found anywhere (only the ambient crackle, sound.tsv 0x51) - "screaming" in the old claim is unconfirmed/likely wrong. **Gating, confirmed by direct comparison**: entry via the blast-push code (`0x50B740`, `test BYTE PTR [+0x7A],0x1`) only fires this for a pushed person when the BLAST INSTANCE's own `+0x7A` bit 0x1 is set - confirmed SET by Firestorm's own impact blast (`0x511800`, write at `0x511967`, `or BYTE PTR [eax+0x7A],1` right after creating its class-7/type-1 blast object) and confirmed NOT set by Lightning's own companion blast (`0x511AE0`, the equivalent alloc+field-setup block at `0x511C20`-`0x511C56` never touches `+0x7A`, and `alloc_unit`/0x4ED8A0 zeroes it by default) - i.e. **Firestorm's blast genuinely does force this run on its victims; Lightning's own companion blast genuinely does not**, a real difference, not a trace gap. Entry via the burning-building eviction path (`0x408AB0`/`0x408B39`) is UNCONDITIONAL (that path sets the state directly via the standard `0x4ED6F0`/`0x4ED640` state-transition pair, never passing through `0x50B740`'s own `+0x7A` gate at all) - every evicted occupant gets the forced run, matching open-populous's existing "Burning building" trace's "and panics" wording exactly as originally written. Not re-checked this session: whether Blast's own spell-cast blast (as opposed to Firestorm/Volcano's fireball-created one) sets `+0x7A` too.

name: Swamp's one-tick "about to die"

name: blocked (stuck on terrain its type can't cross; misnamed "actively preaching" by an earlier draft)
role: **Correction, separate session, trigger now fully confirmed (live-play cross-check: a unit visibly halts in an arms-up pose on steep terrain, then starts losing life after a while - matches exactly)**. Entry: the generic "take one movement step" helper (`0x4EA920`, used everywhere - ordinary walking, preach's approach, go_into_building) calls `0x4EA970` (an 8-slot-cached "is this step blocked" check, almost certainly the per-type `WALK_ALT_DIFF2` terrain-height-difference test - movement profile table `0x5A7B90+0x10`, "how much height change this type can climb") and, if blocked, sets `unit+0x13` bit 0x10 - `order_execute`'s own shared tail (`0x432590`) and a sibling helper (`0x432260`, called from `init_unit_class_1`) both read this exact flag and transition the unit straight into state 33 instead of continuing its order normally. This state's own per-turn handler (0x4D9650) does NOT reference a preacher, a candidate, or anything preach-specific anywhere - it is rhythm-gated (every 8 ticks, the same cadence as invisible/shield/bloodlust/hypnotised): a grace timer (`+0x70`) climbs by 7 per qualifying tick toward a ceiling (flat 32 under the debug/cheat flag, else `0x160`/`0x360` picked by an unidentified per-tribe byte at `tribe+0xC1F`) - once at the ceiling, instead of climbing further it deals 56 life damage every 8 ticks (skippable by a global cheat flag), matching "after a while they start losing life". Its own substate machine (0-3) tries up to 8 waypoints to escape (`0x4EA920` again - re-checking the SAME blocked-step logic per attempt, via the per-type `WALK_ALT_DIFF2`/movement-profile-flag-0x18 branch, or a packed passability/visibility bitmap at `0x96AA74` when that profile flag is clear), falling back to the per-type default (table `0x5A7064`) on several exits. The two real class-1 setters of this state (`0x4324A2`/`order_execute`'s own tail and `0x432CFF`/`0x432260`) are both this exact blocked-flag check, not generic order-dispatch machinery as first guessed, and not preach-specific either way (a third raw setter, `0x512A31`, is a false positive - it belongs to the LAVA FLOW class-7 effect's own init, effect type 34/state 33, a completely different state-number space that happens to share the number 33). 0x4D83B0 (the conversion roll) accepting striker state ∈ {10, 33} as a precondition therefore just means "the striker is either ordinarily carrying out its order, or has momentarily gotten stuck on terrain mid-approach" - not evidence that state 33 itself means "preaching".

name: noticing something
role: Set on BOTH units of a "notice" pairing (a scenery type-9 "head", an unidentified vehicle type, or a different-tribe person, 18.75% chance) found during state 6's walk to the shore; cross-linked via `+0x72` like state 5's own binding. Own per-turn handler untraced - what it actually leads to is open.

name: shaman muster (trigger unidentified)
role: **Corrects this row's own earlier guess**: a live memory trace this session (watch_guard2/3/4.txt) proved this is NOT what the G keybind ("guard the shaman", shortcuts.md) does - G's real mechanism is `person_states.tsv`-unrelated, see `functions.tsv`'s `0x443B40` row (order kind 30/0x1E, a continuous "stay near a reference" escort order given directly to selected followers, nothing to do with this state). This state's own code is real and left traced below, just with an unidentified trigger (whatever sets a tribe's shaman's own person-state directly to 38 was not re-examined once G was ruled out). Entered by having a tribe's own shaman (tribe_struct+0x89D) person-state set directly to 38, with a target position stashed in her own +0x4F and a mode-bit+count byte in +0xA8 (by some still-unknown caller - the commands.tsv `tribe_cmd 0x6E`/`ui_cmd 0x6D` pair that writes exactly these same two fields remains a plausible but unconfirmed candidate, see those rows). Sub-state 0: walks toward +0x4F (snapping to a nearby building's door point via 0x4044B0 if relevant, the same snap used by order kind 0x1D and preach_order_handler), validates the destination every 4th tick (0x4C24F0, the shared "can I go/build there" check), then advances to sub-state 1 or 2 depending on the +0xA8 mode bit. Sub-state 1: on arrival, transitions into a per-type "settled" state (state 39's own row, picked by the per-type fallback table 0x5A7064, overridden to 39 specifically for a shaman when the debug/option flag 0x89D17C bit 0x2 is set) - reads as "stand guard here". Sub-state 2: instead runs further bookkeeping through several unread spell/mana-table functions (0x4C29A0/0x4C2B40/0x4C2B60/0x4C2A50) and allocates a companion/marker object through the same pending-handoff pipeline (global 0x892443) used by spirit-rise and patrol-point markers (0x4BA9B0) - not traced to completion.
